setup: CREATE TABLE items AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS item_id, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'][1 + i] AS kind FROM range(4) t(i)
CREATE TABLE buys AS SELECT i::BIGINT AS buy_id, (i % 8)::BIGINT AS user_id, ((i * 3) % 4)::BIGINT AS item_id, TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' + to_days((i * 5)::INTEGER) AS ts FROM range(120) t(i)
input.pql: PREDICT LIST_DISTINCT(buys.item_id, 0, 30, days) RANK TOP 2 FOR EACH users.user_id

expect.today: recorded at the reference 6298913c on DuckDB, SQLite and Postgres: asked as one binary classification per candidate (COUNT(buys.* WHERE buys.item_id=<c>, 0, 30, days) > 0), one call each, three calls; the scripted endpoint answers no probabilities, so the ranking has no score to order by and is refused INTERNAL_ERROR at predict, naming candidate 0

why: A ranking over named candidates (RANK TOP 2, candidates=): its decomposition into one binary question per candidate, each payload compared, and the refusal of an answer without probabilities; top_k from the query
source: T2.8 ranking end to end (the design rows T2.8a and T2.8b), the reference at 6298913c
